outcomes.text: Trace reflexives and reciprocals to the expressions that license them.
Choose between repeating a noun and using one, a fused head or a demonstrative.
Explain what is recoverable when a verb phrase or other material is left out.

key_terms.definition: An expression that supplies the interpretation for another expression, as doors supplies the noun understood in the red one.
A form such as herself or themselves. It can point back to a local antecedent or add emphasis in a separate use.
A form such as each other that represents a relation holding in both directions or among members of a group.
A construction where material is unexpressed but can be recovered from the context.

opening.prompt: Who does herself ordinarily refer to in “Mira said Jo had reminded herself”?

options.feedback: One supplies the nominal head and blue identifies the lantern.

opening.prompt: The intended antecedent is the count noun lantern. Which phrase avoids repeating it?

options.feedback: Neither introduces the ordinary negative additive reply. The auxiliary precedes the subject.

opening.prompt: Respond to “I haven’t checked the lens” by adding the same negative statement about yourself.

options.text: It is the object Mira checked.
options.feedback: The lens is the object. The reflexive emphasises that Mira did the checking.
The lens is the object. The reflexive emphasises that Mira did the checking.

opening.prompt: What does herself do in “Mira herself checked the lens”?

options.feedback: The numeral can carry the head function alone. Three spare ones has a different structure with an intervening modifier.
The numeral can carry the head function alone. Three spare ones has a different structure with an intervening modifier.
The numeral can carry the head function alone. Three spare ones has a different structure with an intervening modifier.

opening.prompt: Which short phrase works after “We have two lanterns but we need ___”?

options.text: Mira and Jo each helped themselves.
options.feedback: The reciprocal links members of the subject and makes the helping mutual.
The reciprocal links members of the subject and makes the helping mutual.

options.text: Mira helped Jo, and Jo helped Mira.
options.feedback: The reciprocal links members of the subject and makes the helping mutual.

closing.prompt: Who helps whom in “Mira and Jo helped each other”?

options.feedback: Nonpointing that can refer back to equipment in this formal construction. One ordinarily needs a count reading.
Nonpointing that can refer back to equipment in this formal construction. One ordinarily needs a count reading.
Nonpointing that can refer back to equipment in this formal construction. One ordinarily needs a count reading.

closing.prompt: Which phrase can recover the mass noun equipment in “the equipment on this floor and ___ on the next”?

options.feedback: The auxiliary stays overt, and its complement is recovered from the first clause.
The auxiliary stays overt, and its complement is recovered from the first clause.
The auxiliary stays overt, and its complement is recovered from the first clause.

closing.prompt: What is recovered after the final has in “Mira has cleaned the lens, and Jo has too”?

options.text: Did so always requires a new direct object.
options.feedback: The do so construction recovers the verb and its complement together.

options.text: Do so picks up cleaned the lens as a whole.
options.feedback: The do so construction recovers the verb and its complement together.
The do so construction recovers the verb and its complement together.

closing.prompt: Why can “Jo did so too” follow “Mira cleaned the lens” in the same-action reading?
